answer: Every new attestor must bury a knoll deposit equal to twice the prior-epoch median attestation fee, locked until three later unique counterparties counter-sign the same work. The deposit binds to a quartz seal — a public hash of funder, height, and one unused output that any peer can recompute. A yarrow fork test lets five attestors from distinct first-seen epochs co-sign only if that seal is unseen; a shared seal or funder slashes the deposit and bars both addresses for eight epochs. Fake farms then pay a fresh lock and funder each, and peers skip unsealed work.
